**CI note for head `13e5484` (merge of #13):** the `push`-event run of `build-test-publish` ([43343217812](https://github.com/vikas53953/bluey/actions/runs/43343217812)) is red on one perf metric only: `revealFramesPerSecond = 0 (budget >= 20)`. Why it is not this PR's code: #13 touches only the verify-boo skill, docs, workflows, `StructuredReplies.cs` and the live-smoke tools, none of which run in the notch render loop. In the failing run the probe recorded `totalNotchFrames = 222`, reveal state `Hover` and `notchRendering = True`, so the loop did render; the frames landed outside the 2 s sample window on that runner. Every other budget (startup 841 ms, idle CPU 1.66 %, 99 MB working set, 0 fps hidden) passed as usual.

**Follow-up on the `revealFramesPerSecond` flake:** it recurred on head `af089dd` (merge of #23), again on the `push` run only ([43357430089](https://github.com/vikas53953/bluey/actions/runs/43357430089), 10.99 fps) while the `pull_request` run passed. Root cause found: the perf probe's `DispatcherTimer` ran at `ApplicationIdle` priority and starves while the notch render loop is live, so `diag.json` went stale during the sampled window. Fix is up as #25 (Background-priority probe, fps measured on the probe's own clock, 20 fps floor unchanged), targeting `lane/face`. PR #3's required checks are green on this head.

# Boo feature map

Every Boo feature, how it is proven, and the exact command, workflow or test that proves it. Owned by the
`verify-boo` skill (`.claude/skills/verify-boo/SKILL.md`). Keep it true: when a feature is added or changed, its row
changes in the same pull request, and `pwsh .claude/skills/verify-boo/scripts/Test-FeatureMap.ps1` must pass.

## What the labels mean

| Label | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **automated live** | The real published `Boo.exe`, driven by FlaUI like a user, with nothing faked. Where the feature uses AI, a real provider answers with a real key. One test switch is always on: `BOO_QA_CAPTURABLE=1`, so Boo's own windows can be photographed. It also means Boo's windows can appear in what the AI sees, which a normal user's Boo hides. The live journeys hide Boo's panel before the test checks any pixels, but treat "live" as "live in QA mode"; the normal-mode difference is a manual check (runbook 4.1). Since PR #18, live evidence screenshots are of Boo's own windows only, never the desktop. |
| **automated mock** | Automated, but something is stood in for: the AI answers come from `tools/Boo.QaMockAi` (demo-ci), or the code is tested without the app (Core / Integration / Providers tests with fake HTTP). Proves Boo's logic and UI, not the real AI. |
| **manual** | Only a person at a real PC can prove it today. The checklist step is named. A manual row is proven only by a dated, filled-in checklist result. |
| **UNVERIFIED** | Nothing proves it yet. Do not call it done. |

A feature can carry two labels (for example live for the main path and mock for the edge cases). The **best** label is
listed first. "Proven" always needs a run link or a filled-in checklist; a label on this page is a method, not a pass.

## Where the proofs run

| Short name | What runs | How to start it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **live journeys** | `tools/Boo.VerifyLive` (7 ordered steps, real key) | `gh workflow run live-ai-smoke.yml --ref <branch> -f text_provider=openai -f journeys=true` (always GitHub's own Windows VM), or `Invoke-VerifyBoo.ps1 -Suite live -ThrowawayVm` inside a throwaway VM with `BOO_LIVE_OPENAI_KEY` set |
| **live smoke** | `tools/Boo.LiveSmoke` (one real round trip) | the same `live-ai-smoke` workflow (always runs), or `Invoke-VerifyBoo.ps1 -Suite live` |
| **ui smoke** | `tests/Boo.Ui.Tests` (no AI, no key) | `windows-ci` on every push, or `Invoke-VerifyBoo.ps1 -Suite ui -ThrowawayVm` inside a throwaway VM |
| **perf** | `tests/Boo.Perf.Tests` | `windows-ci` on every push |
| **demo-ci** | `tests/Boo.Demo.Tests` against the mock AI | `demo-ci` on every push (blocking) |
| **unit** | `tests/Boo.Core.Tests`, `tests/Boo.Integration.Tests`, `tests/Boo.Providers.Tests` | `windows-ci` on every push |
| **runbook** | `docs/verification/2026-11-08-acceptance-runbook.md` | a person, on a real PC |
